newsitem.title: USA: Bellwether will sell 10 pct of new wells.
newsitem.headline: Bellwether will sell 10 pct of new wells.

text.p: Bellwether Exploration Co will sell the bottom 10 percent of the wells it acquired in the $142-million acquisition of oil properties owned by limited partnerships, which closed early this month.

"We are well positioned to withstand any price change relative to the competition. The disposal will reduce our debt to capital ratio from 64 percent to the mid-50s," Chief Financial Officer Chuck Green told the 1997 IPAA Oil and Gas Investment Symposium Wednesday.
The deal increased Bellwether's reserves to 40.1 million barrels from 7.3 million, Green said.
Looking forward, he said 80 to 85 percent of what will be required to produce a growth rate for the company of 10 to 15 percent is already identified.

Green said a 4 to 5 percent change in oil and gas prices would produce a 4 to 5 percent change in the company's cash flow per share and EBITDA (earnings before interest taxes depreciation and amortization).
Green said the company has a virtually unused $19 million credit facility which could be used to fund acquisitions.
